ops.why: At the fork below the camp, where the Mile House track meets the Swampmoth Town track, a post carries two boards: the low one south-west toward the Mile House, the high one north toward Swampmoth Town.
The spring-fed tarn below the bench, where the column draws its water.
The serjeant stands at his tent's mouth, where the column reports and the levy is counted.
The serjeant keeps his own tent's mouth after dark.
The serjeant commands what is left of the column from the command tent.

The man on watch stands in the gap in the stakes and asks for the levy. 2.7b11p: the gap is in the stake line on the camp path, where the chunk ground (76.48 m) and the survey ground (76.46 m) agree; the old spot sat beside the barricade on the slope toward the water, where his feet hovered at the stakes.
The column eats what it has at the fire.
The column sits out the night on the bench by the fire.

ops.role: what is left of the column
ops.why: The column keeps the watch on the track and the fire on the bench.
The pay book in the command tent, with the last entry in it.
The toll office's published schedules, copied out and kept with the pay book.
The duty roster nailed to the aspen in the gap of the palisade below the tents, kept up in a clerk's hand.
The roster tree in the gap of the palisade, where LF21's parley over the pardon is held.

lootTable.storyNote: The last of the meal, a hand deep at the bottom of the sack.

ops.why: The column's food, nearly gone.

lootTable.storyNote: Water carried up from the stream.

ops.why: Water for the line.
A flower in the clearing; its buds dry for the healer's shelf. (vanilla:plants/floramountainflower01blue, chunk_2_6_vegetation.bin#213:0)
Crow den at the roster tree. A dead tree by a road where carrion lies.
Marsh Rat den at the camp midden. The rats nest inside a big carcass or a rubbish heap.
Hackwing den at snags on the slope below the bench. A dead-tree roost over open marsh with long sight lines over prey.
What the column carried off when it walked out of its fort: spare blades kept against the serjeant's side of the tent.
The column's spare Legion kit, kept under the serjeant's eye so no man sells it on the track.
Where the Blackwood Road leaves its last straight from Gideon and turns west between two rises. A loaded cart slows here. The column comes down off the hill to meet it.
On the Blackwood Road out of Gideon, the last straight before the bend. A traveller who stops here sees the bend ahead, where the column takes its levy.
The deserters keep a hidden canoe on their spring-fed tarn above the road.
